claims.text: ASP.NET Core middleware registered with app.Use... calls runs in the exact order those calls appear in Program.cs.
A middleware can run code both before it calls the next delegate and after that call returns.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Middleware: write custom middleware

claims.text: A middleware short-circuits the pipeline by not calling the next delegate, usually after writing a response itself; nothing registered after it then runs for that request.

For an endpoint marked [Authorize], app.UseAuthorization() stops the request instead of calling next when it is not permitted; the 401/403 is produced by the scheme it challenges, not by the authorization middleware directly.

In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, wiring calls run in this order: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, RequestLoggingMiddleware, UseCors, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, MapControllers; ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is first among Đơn Hàng's own calls only, not the whole pipeline.
RequestLoggingMiddleware starts a stopwatch, calls next(context), then logs the method, path, response status code, and elapsed time after next returns.

Sending POST /api/v1/orders to the running stage-1 lab with no Authorization header returns 401, and docker compose logs api shows a RequestLoggingMiddleware line for that request reporting status 401.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: docker compose logs api after curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders

claims.text: ASP.NET Core's routing matches an incoming request to an endpoint before any user-registered middleware runs; the matched endpoint's delegate is invoked only after every middleware in the pipeline has run without short-circuiting.

If RequestLoggingMiddleware were registered after UseAuthorization instead of before it, a request rejected by UseAuthorization would short-circuit before RequestLoggingMiddleware ever called next, so it would not be logged.
